claims.text: Post-processing additively manufactured HfNbTaTiZr with deep cryogenic treatment improves dimensional precision.
Deep cryogenic treatment improves the mechanical integrity and strength–ductility balance of additively manufactured HfNbTaTiZr.
Deep cryogenic treatment reduces fabrication-induced defects in additively manufactured HfNbTaTiZr.
The components are produced by laser melting deposition.
As-deposited HfNbTaTiZr components exhibit residual stresses.
As-deposited HfNbTaTiZr components exhibit distortion.
As-deposited HfNbTaTiZr components contain fabrication-induced defects.
The deep cryogenic treatment uses a long immersion time and is applied immediately after additive manufacturing.
Laser melting deposition and deep cryogenic treatment can be combined to process HfNbTaTiZr.
The relevant alloy composition is Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr.
Deep cryogenic treatment induces a phase transition in the additively manufactured alloy.
The induced phase transition forms HCP phases.
Deep cryogenic treatment increases precipitates near grain boundaries.
Lattice-distortion adjustments caused by deep cryogenic treatment produce stress relaxation and microstructural homogenization.
Deep cryogenic treatment consumes residual stress by promoting lattice distortion and targeted phase transitions.
Grain-boundary precipitates reduce fabrication-induced defects.
Stress relaxation limits post-deposition deformation and therefore reduces dimensional deviations.
Relative to the as-deposited state, deep cryogenic treatment increases tensile strength by approximately 11–25%.
Deep cryogenic treatment increases elongation relative to the as-deposited state.
The expected benefits extend to similar high-entropy-alloy compositions produced by laser additive manufacturing.

contradictions.description: The un-subscripted formula HfNbTaTiZr ordinarily denotes an equiatomic alloy, whereas the conditions specify non-equiatomic Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr. It is unclear which composition is the actual baseline and test material.

The predicted outcome presents an approximately 11–25% tensile-strength increase relative to the as-deposited baseline, but the evidence assigns 11% to the as-deposited comparison and 25% to an as-cast comparison.
